info.title: edifact — read and validate UN/EDIFACT against the published directories
info.description: The `edifact` command line tool: ingest a UN/EDIFACT directory distribution into a pack, inspect what a pack holds, and validate or project an interchange against it. Install with `dotnet tool install --global Edifact.Cli`.

commands.name: ingest
commands.description:
Read a UNECE release directory into a compiled pack.
--out <directory>             Where packs are written. Default: as resolved below.
--syntax <directory>          Where the ISO 9735 definitions live.
--no-strict                   Write a pack even if something went unaccounted for.
--include-prose               Keep the directory's descriptive text. Writes to
<pack-id>-prose, which .gitignore keeps out of the repo.

commands.name: inspect
commands.description:
Print a compiled pack's manifest.
--packs <directory>           Where packs live.

commands.name: project
commands.description:
Write a message type and everything it names.
--pack <pack-id>              Which release. Worked out from UNH for a file;
required for --message.
--packs <directory>           Where packs live.
--syntax <directory>          Where the ISO 9735 definitions live.
--guide <path>                An implementation guide to layer over the release.
Repeatable; the order is the precedence order.
--xml                         Write XML rather than JSON. Interchanges only: a
linked message type has no XML form.
--out <directory>             Write one file per message there rather than to
standard output. Required for an interchange holding
more than one message.

commands.name: validate
commands.description:
Read an interchange and report what is wrong with it.
--pack <pack-id>              Which release to validate against. Default: whichever
one UNH says the interchange was written against.
--packs <directory>           Where packs live.
--syntax <directory>          Where the ISO 9735 definitions live.
--guide <path>                An implementation guide to layer over the release.
Repeatable; the order is the precedence order.
--tree                        Print each message's structure as well.
--quiet                       Report only errors, not warnings.
--round-trip                  Also write the interchange back out and report whether
it is reproduced character for character.
